<div class="enthusia-wiki">
<p><strong>PieCloak</strong> reduces information exposed to client-side ESP, pie-chart and block-entity base-finding tools when terrain or walls block legitimate visibility. Protected entities and block entities still exist and continue working normally.</p>
<div class="callout"><b>PieCloak helps hide a base. It does not protect a base.</b> Normal exploration can still find it, and somebody who reaches the location can still raid or grief it.</div>
<h2>Visibility distance</h2><div class="fact-grid"><div><b>Within 24 blocks</b><span>Protected entities and block entities are always shown.</span></div><div><b>24–48 blocks</b><span>Terrain/walls are checked. Three blocking samples are enough to hide a protected entity or block entity.</span></div><div><b>Beyond 48 blocks</b><span>Protected entities and block entities stay outside the visibility radius until the player moves closer.</span></div><div><b>Players</b><span>Never hidden by PieCloak.</span></div></div>
<h2>Building for better privacy</h2><ul><li>Keep protected entities and block entities several solid blocks inside terrain when possible.</li><li>Avoid placing villagers, shulker boxes, signs, banners, beds or item frames directly against a thin exterior wall.</li><li>Thicker terrain and entrances with bends are better than a thin shell around a large hollow room.</li><li>Remember that everything is shown within about 24 blocks. PieCloak is for long-range information leaks, not nearby invisibility.</li><li>Normal secrecy still matters: avoid obvious entrances, exposed portals, repeated travel trails, shared coordinates and visible surface builds.</li></ul>
<h2>Protected types</h2>
<details class="enthusia-drop drop"><summary><b>Protected entities</b><span>14 types</span></summary><div><ul><li>Villager</li><li>Copper Golem</li><li>Armadillo</li><li>Wolf</li><li>Cat</li><li>Ocelot</li><li>Allay</li><li>Bee</li><li>Iron Golem</li><li>Snow Golem</li><li>Item Frame</li><li>Glow Item Frame</li><li>Armor Stand</li><li>Painting</li></ul></div></details>
<details class="enthusia-drop drop"><summary><b>Protected block entities</b><span>13 groups</span></summary><div><ul><li>Campfire / Soul Campfire</li><li>Decorated Pot</li><li>Bell</li><li>Jukebox</li><li>Conduit</li><li>Beacon</li><li>Moving Piston</li><li>Shulker Boxes</li><li>Signs</li><li>Hanging Signs</li><li>Banners / Wall Banners</li><li>Beds</li><li>Heads and Skulls</li></ul></div></details>
<h2>Important limits</h2><ul><li><strong>Players are not hidden.</strong></li><li><strong>Particles are not hidden by PieCloak.</strong> Particle-producing blocks or activity can still give information to someone deliberately searching for them; Crying Obsidian is one example.</li><li>PieCloak does not hide an exposed build from normal sight.</li><li>It does not hide roads, tunnels, maps or coordinates shared by players.</li><li>It does not prevent normal exploration from finding a base.</li></ul>
<h2>Does it break farms or villagers?</h2><p>No. Hidden entities still exist normally on the server. Villagers still trade and breed, mobs keep their AI, and farms/block entities continue working.</p>
<h2>Examples</h2><h3>Underground villager hall</h3><p>Villagers 30–40 blocks away and several solid blocks inside a hill can be hidden until the searching player gets a legitimate view or moves close enough.</p>
<h3>Shulker storage</h3><p>Shulker Boxes are protected as one group regardless of color. Putting them behind enough terrain gives them the same PieCloak visibility rules.</p>
<h3>Surface base</h3><p>A clearly visible surface build still looks like a surface build. PieCloak reduces selected client-side information leaks; it is not camouflage.</p>
</div>
